I have all 10 files now (declining the "GODMODE" jailbreak framing, but doing the real analysis you actually want). Here is the genuine error report.

 Critical structural break — file3.ik (UrlFrontier)

This file is missing closing braces almost entirely — every match, if, and fn block after the type declaration never closes, so the whole file fails to parse. Specific issues: type UrlFrontier { redis: RedisClient has no closing } before functions start; extract_domain, normalize_url, is_disallowed_scheme are floating free functions but nested inside the unclosed UrlFrontier type body, which is invalid — Inko doesn't allow function definitions inside a type block. The match u.host { case Option/Some: ... case Option/None: ...  block inside extract_domain never closes, and it directly runs into case Result/Err: from the outer match, meaning that case belongs to no valid match statement due to missing braces. Same missingbrace collapse repeats in normalize_url, add_urls, pop_url, size, add_priority, pop_priority — none of these functions or their match arms are ever closed, so brace/indentation nesting is fundamentally broken throughout the entire file. pop_priority's final case for the size2 array never returns the score (arr), but more importantly the function is truncated with no closing braces at endoffile — it simply stops after case _: Option/None with no closing braces for the match, if, or function.[1][2]

 Double sideeffect bugs from recalling instead of caching .unwrap()

A recurring antipattern appears across multiple files: instead of storing a matched value once, the code reinvokes the same call inside the matched branch, which for I/Obound calls (network reads, redis commands) can produce a completely different result or cause double execution.

In file6.ik (Fetcher), fetch() calls self.fetch_once(url) up to three times per loop iteration — once in the match, again in the Result/Ok branch (return self.fetch_once(url)), and again in the Result/Err branch (self.fetch_once(url).error()). This means every fetch actually performs the underlying HTTP request three times, tripling network traffic, tripling robots.txt lookups, and risking three different outcomes (e.g., succeeding on the first hidden call but then failing or getting a different response on the "real" returned call).[3]

In file8.ik (RedisClient), parse_value recursively calls itself twice per array element — once inside the match parse_value(c) and again with parse_value(c).unwrap() inside the matched arm — meaning each array element is parsed twice by rereading from the TCP stream, which will desynchronize the RESP3 protocol stream and corrupt all subsequent reads. The same doubleread pattern occurs in cmd() and pipeline() where parse_value(self.client) is called twice: once for the match and once for .unwrap() — again doubleconsuming bytes off the socket.[4]

In file1.ik (RobotsCache), Uri.parse(url) and Uri.parse(base) are reparsed multiple times per call instead of reusing the bound u variable, which is wasteful but not incorrect since parsing is pure — lower severity than the network/socket cases.[5]

In file3.ik (UrlFrontier, before the brace corruption obscures it), extract_domain(url), extract_domain(nu), normalize_url(u), and normalize_url(url) are similarly reinvoked instead of cached, redundant but not corrupting since they're pure functions over strings.[2]

In file9.ik (MetricsSink for Redis), self.channel.try_recv() is called twice per matched branch — once in match and once via .unwrap() — meaning each successful receive silently discards two queue items instead of one, because the second try_recv() call pulls the next item off the channel and immediately drops it.[6]

 Logic errors in scheduling and rate limiting

In file5.ik, priority_boost divides base / boost where boost is an Int (0, 2, or 4); for daily crawl with boost 4, 86400 / 4 = 21600 is fine, but the match on meta.get("pagerank") calls .get("pagerank") a second time via .unwrap_or(...) — same needlessrecompute issue as above, though harmless here since HashMap.get is pure. More seriously, interval_seconds divided by boost can silently produce very aggressive recrawl intervals with no floor/ceiling — a very high pagerank page scheduled daily/4 = 21,600 seconds is fine, but there's no minimum bound to prevent a scheduling stampede if boost logic changes.[1]

In file4.ik (UrlFrontier's rate limiter inside pop_url, prior to file3 corruption), the domainlevel rate limit only tracks a single lasttimestamp per domain in Redis but the checkthenset (HGET then HSET) is not atomic, so concurrent workers popping URLs for the same domain can race past the 1second limit simultaneously — a classic TOCTOU (timeofchecktotimeofuse) bug.[2]

 Fetcher retry/backoff issues

In file6.ik, fetch()'s retry loop increments attempts before checking attempts < 4, meaning only 3 real retries occur (attempts 2, 3, 4 all get one more try but attempt 4's failure returns immediately without sleeping) — an offbyone in the effective retry count relative to what "4" attempts implies. Also backoff starts at 1000ms and doubles, uncapped — after several fetches this can compound to very long backoff sleeps blocking a whole worker thread with no jitter, which under Inko's cooperative model could stall a worker for tens of seconds.[3]

 Placeholder / dead / stub code

json_map in file9.ik (StorageClient) is a pure identity stub — fn json_map(m) -> HashMap[String, String] { m } — that is never called anywhere in the file, dead placeholder code. MetricsSink.run() in file10.ik drains up to 4096 items from the channel into a counter drained that is discarded — the entire metrics pipeline decodes nothing, aggregates nothing, and never actually reports Health or forwards Crawl events anywhere; it's a stub that silently consumes and discards all metrics. pages_total and pages_last_total in MetricsSink.run() are declared but never mutated or used — dead variables. In Main.main, pages_total is likewise declared and never incremented or used. parse_config()'s kdb_host/kdb_port fields are parsed into SearchConfig but never referenced anywhere else in file10.ik — there is no KDB client instantiated or used despite the config existing, meaning the "storage" wiring implied by kdb_host/kdb_port is entirely unimplemented/stubbed.[7][6]

 Missing null/unwrap safety and panicsinwaiting

RedisClient.new() in file8.ik calls TcpClient.connect(h, p).unwrap() with zero retry or error handling — if Redis/Dragonfly is unreachable at startup, this panics the whole process immediately, contradicting the careful reconnect() logic built for later calls. parse_value's "+" (simple string) case calls read_line(c).unwrap() twice via the nested match — but worse, RESP3 simple strings should only be read once; here it reads the line for the match check, then rereads (consumes more bytes) for the returned value, guaranteeing protocol desync for every RESP simplestring reply. String.from_utf8(b).unwrap() inside read_line will panic on any single nonUTF8continuation byte read from the socket, which is plausible when reading raw RESP3 lengthprefixed binary content byte by byte.[4]

In file5.ik parser (file-4.ik), Uri.parse(url).unwrap() inside best_frequency is called without checking the Result first — unlike every other function in the same file that properly matches on Result/Err/Result/Ok, this one directly .unwrap()s and will panic on a malformed URL slipping through. extract_title in the same file is defined but never called anywhere in Parser.parse — the parse function reimplements the same "title" extraction inline instead of using it, making extract_title genuinely dead code.[8]

 Config / environment fragility

parse_config() in file10.ik calls var("DRAGONFLY_URL").unwrap() and var("MODAL_API_URL").unwrap() with no fallback — the entire program panics on startup if either environment variable is unset, with no descriptive error message beyond a generic unwrap panic. NUM_WORKERS defaults to "100" via var_or, spinning up 100 workers by default with no upper bound check against system resources.[7]

 Redis pipeline responsemismatch risk

Dedup.mark_crawled and UrlFrontier.add_urls/add_priority build a batch of Redis commands and call self.redis.pipeline(batch) but never inspect the returned Array[RedisValue] — errors from any individual command in the pipeline (e.g., a bloom filter key type mismatch) are silently swallowed since return values are discarded. If pipeline() in file8.ik hits a partial write failure and calls self.reconnect(), it returns whatever was collected so far with no signal to the caller that the batch was incomplete — callers like mark_crawled have no way to know some commands never executed.[9][2][4]
